name: truncated-run-reported-as-completed
description: ADMITTED GAP: a well-formed stream that simply stops is consumed without complaint — the TypeScript client resolves `runAgent()` with a settlement a completed run is indistinguishable from, and the .NET converter iterates to the end and throws nothing — where the specification says a truncated run has no outcome and MUST NOT be reported as having succeeded; this pins what both reference clients do today, silently, so the gap cannot change unnoticed
kill: give either client an end-of-stream check that requires a terminal event — one of the two surfacings the spec permits, the other being to leave the run unresolved — and it makes this fixture fail. That is deliberate: this fixture pins today's gap, not the rule. Anyone landing that check MUST update this fixture in the same change, on the lane that landed it: `outcome` to `failed` with an `errorContains` where the client raises a synthetic failure, or an `expectOverrides.<lane>` block with an `intentional` reason where the other client still consumes the stream quietly — flipping the base alone reddens the lane that has no check, and #2354, the open fix, is TypeScript-only. `messageCount` and `messages` stay either way, because the same spec sentence that forbids reporting success also says everything the run delivered before the break remains delivered: a client that starts failing the run must not also lose the message, and this fixture is where that is caught. Verified rather than asserted — with #2354's check ported onto main this fixture goes red on `outcome` alone, and the replacement block prescribed above then passes. The stream around the missing terminator is otherwise flawless — the producer declares 1.0, and the message is opened, filled and CLOSED — so the absent terminal event is the ONLY thing that can fail this run. The three other fixtures whose streams carry no terminal event each fail for a different reason the verifier already catches (`first-event-not-run-started-fatal`, `nested-run-started-fatal`, `step-finished-without-start-fatal`), which is why none of them pins this one.

stream.delta: the run that carried it is not

messages.content: this message is complete; the run that carried it is not
